purpose: Adds a 'Host Google Fonts Locally' feature that intercepts Google Fonts requests, downloads CSS and woff2 files, caches them locally, and rewrites URLs to eliminate external DNS lookups and improve GDPR compliance.
riskRationale: The implementation is generally sound and follows codebase conventions, but the v1-to-v2 Google Fonts URL conversion has a critical gap that silently breaks font downloading for users requesting specific font weights/styles, and there are race conditions in concurrent font file downloads.

text: Well-structured feature with clean separation of concerns, graceful degradation, and dual interception (style_loader_tag + buffer). The main concerns are an incomplete v1-to-v2 URL conversion that silently fails for font variants, a streaming download race condition, and aggressive font cache clearing on every full cache purge. Tests cover the basic toggle/submit path but lack failure scenarios for the download step.

reasoning: The v1-to-v2 URL conversion silently fails for font weight/style variants — a core functionality gap that must be fixed before merge. Race condition in concurrent font downloads and aggressive font cache clearing on every full purge are also important concerns.

message: Clean separation of concerns — the Google_Fonts class is a standalone unit with clearly named public methods (process_style_tag, process_buffer, download_and_rewrite, clear_font_cache) that integrate naturally with existing plugin architecture.
Graceful degradation: when download_and_rewrite fails ('' === $local_url), the original tag is returned unchanged, ensuring fonts always load even when local hosting fails.
Buffer-level interception acts as a safety net for @import and inline <link> patterns that bypass the style_loader_tag filter, ensuring comprehensive coverage.
Font cache invalidation on setting toggle correctly handles both enable and disable transitions, with proper state management.

V1-to-v2 Google Fonts URL conversion is incomplete. The v1 API uses ':weight' syntax (e.g., 'family=Roboto:400,700') which differs from v2's '@' syntax ('family=Roboto:wght@400;700'). The code blindly passes v1 query params to the /css2 endpoint, which will fail for any URL specifying font weights or styles. This silently breaks font downloading for the most common Google Fonts use cases, and the user's pages still load fonts from Google's servers (GDPR non-compliance) despite the toggle being enabled.
suggestion: Parse the 'family' parameter value in v1 URLs and convert weight/style syntax to v2 format. For simple cases (family name only, no weights), the current pass-through works. For weights/styles, convert ':400,700' to 'wght@400;700' and ':ital,wght@...' appropriately. Alternatively, avoid the conversion entirely and use the v1 API endpoint (/css) directly instead of converting to /css2.

message: Race condition in download_font_file with streaming writes. Two concurrent requests for the same font file both pass the file_exists() check and start streaming downloads to the same destination path. If one download fails, it deletes the file that the other request may have successfully written, causing the font cache to be corrupted.
suggestion: Use an atomic write pattern: download to a temporary file first, then rename to the final destination. Use a file lock or a marker file to signal that a download is in progress to prevent concurrent downloads of the same font.

message: Google_Fonts::clear_font_cache() is called on every full cache purge (delete_all_cache_files). This means every cache clear — triggered by permalink changes, theme switches, settings saves, plugin activate/deactivate — forces all Google Fonts to be re-downloaded on the next page load. This creates a burst of external HTTP requests (20-40+ for typical multi-weight font setups) and significantly slows the first uncached page view.
suggestion: Make font cache clearing opt-in by removing it from delete_all_cache_files(). Instead, only clear font cache when the hostGoogleFontsLocally setting toggles (already handled in Main::on_settings_update) or add a separate 'Clear Font Cache' action button in the UI.
suggestionCode:
// Remove this line from delete_all_cache_files()
// Google_Fonts::clear_font_cache();

message: A new Google_Fonts instance is created on every buffer process call, even though Main::setup_hooks already creates one for the style_loader_tag filter. This means two separate instances exist per page load, each with its own copy of options, file cache dir, etc.
suggestion: Inject the existing Google_Fonts instance into the Cache class via a setter, similar to how Image_Optimisation is injected. Cache already has set_image_optimisation() as a precedent. Alternatively, store the Google_Fonts instance as a Main class property and pass it to Cache's constructor.

message: The submit test for hostGoogleFontsLocally uses apiCall.mockResolvedValueOnce({ success: true }) without a 'message' field, unlike other tests in the same file that include it. While the component falls back to the default successMessage, the inconsistency means the test doesn't verify the notification message for the Google Fonts toggle path.
suggestion: Include a 'message' field in the resolved value for consistency with other tests and to verify notification rendering.
